title: Hyphens in Prefixed Words
keyIdea: A hyphen is a short dash that joins words or parts of words. Most prefixes join straight on (rebuild, rearrange, misspell), but add a hyphen when the prefix ends with the same vowel the root word starts with (re-enter, co-own, re-elect), and when the hyphen tells two different words apart: recover means get well, re-cover means cover again. Two or more words that work together as one describing word before a noun are joined with hyphens (a man-eating shark, a well-known author, a ten-year-old girl). After the noun they stay apart (the author is well known), and an -ly adverb never takes a hyphen (a brightly lit room).
familyTip: Say a phrase like 'a man eating shark' or 'twenty odd people' out loud and draw both meanings on paper, one with the hyphen and one without. Then hunt for a word on a cereal box or in a book that starts with re-, co- or pre- and decide whether it needs a hyphen.

visual.caption: Is the hyphen choice right? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: The torn sofa was re-covered in red.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: recover or re-cover, join or hyphen, move a hyphen to change meaning, before or after the noun, find the slip.

kid: A hyphen is a short dash. It can join a prefix to a word. Most prefixes join straight on, with no dash: rebuild, misspell.
Some pairs of words look the same but for a hyphen. Gran will recover from her cold means she will get well. We will re-cover the sofa means we will cover it again.

Add a hyphen when the prefix ends with the same vowel that the word starts with. So re and enter make re-enter, and co and own make co-own. But re and arrange make rearrange, as e and a are not the same.
Two words can work as one describing word. Then a hyphen joins them, but only when they come before the noun: a well-known author. After the noun, leave it out: the author is well known.
adult: Ages 10 to 11. The national curriculum in England puts hyphens used to avoid ambiguity in Year 6 (English Appendix 2). Its own examples are man eating shark against man-eating shark, and recover against re-cover. The Year 5 to 6 spelling list adds that a hyphen can join a prefix to a root word. This is most common when the prefix ends with the vowel the root starts with: co-own, re-enter, co-ordinate.

Most prefixed words are written as one word. A hyphen is used to keep two words apart: re-sign and resign, re-cover and recover, re-count and recount. It also splits a doubled vowel. When two or three words act as one describing word before a noun, hyphens show which words go together: a man-eating shark, twenty-odd people, extra-large eggs, a part-time job.

Common mistakes: a hyphen after every prefix (re-build); a doubled vowel run together (reenter); a hyphen after the noun (the author is well-known); a hyphen after an -ly adverb (a brightly-lit room); and only one hyphen in a longer group (an eleven-year old girl). Some words vary by publisher, so check meaning first, then the vowel rule.

In the lab your child picks recover or re-cover in six sentences. They decide join or hyphen for six prefixed words, and move a hyphen, or leave it out, so five phrases match a meaning. Then they check six phrases before and after a noun, and find the hyphen slip in four sentences.

practice.prompt: The tent was ripped, so Dad will ▢ it with a new sheet. Which word fits?
practice.hint: Is the tent getting well, or getting covered again?
practice.explain: re-cover means cover again. recover means get well, which does not fit a tent.

practice.prompt: A describing word is made of {n} words joined together, like ten-year-old. How many hyphens does it need?
practice.hint: One hyphen goes in each gap between two of the words.
practice.explain: {n} words have {=n-1} gaps between them, so {=n-1} hyphens join them into one describing word.

practice.prompt: Which word needs a hyphen after its prefix?
practice.hint: Look for the prefix vowel meeting the same vowel.
practice.explain: In re-elect, e meets e, so a hyphen keeps it easy to read. rebuild and rearrange are joined.

practice.prompt: A list has {w} prefixed words. In {h} of them the prefix vowel meets the same vowel. How many of the words are just joined, with no hyphen?
practice.hint: Only the words where the same vowel meets get a hyphen.
practice.explain: {h} words get a hyphen, so the other {=w-h} are written as one word.

choices: She is a well known singer.
practice.hint: Does the describing pair come before or after the noun?
practice.explain: After the noun, leave out the hyphen. Before it, join it: a well-known singer.

pool.prompt: What does a man-eating shark mean?
choices: A man who is eating shark
A man and a shark eating
pool.hint: The hyphen joins man and eating into one describing word.
pool.explain: man-eating describes the shark: it eats people. With no hyphen, it reads as a man eating shark meat.

pool.hint: Find the prefix that ends with the same vowel its word starts with.
pool.explain: co ends in o and own starts with o, so co-own. misspell and preheat are joined.

pool.prompt: The match was close, so the judges will ▢ the points. Which word fits?
pool.hint: Are they telling a story, or counting again?
pool.explain: re-count means count again. recount means tell what happened.

pool.hint: Think about adverbs that end in -ly, like brightly.
pool.explain: brightly is an -ly adverb, and an -ly adverb never takes a hyphen, so it stays a brightly lit hall.

pool.prompt: How many hyphens are in 'a {n}-year-old cat'? Count the dashes between the words.
pool.hint: The number, year and old are joined into one describing word.
pool.explain: {n}-year-old has a hyphen after {n} and a hyphen after year, so the answer is 2 hyphens.

pool.prompt: Why does re-enter have a hyphen but rearrange does not?
choices: In re-enter the same vowel meets itself.
Every re word needs a hyphen.
pool.hint: Look at the last letter of re and the first letter of each word.
pool.explain: e meets e in re-enter. In rearrange, e meets a, which is a different vowel, so it is joined.
twenty-odd means about twenty. Without the hyphen it reads as twenty strange people.

pool.prompt: Which sentence has a hyphen slip?
pool.hint: Which prefix meets a letter that is not the same vowel?
pool.explain: re meets b in rebuild, so no hyphen is needed. re-enter keeps its hyphen.

pool.prompt: Gran had flu. Which sentence says she got well?
pool.explain: recover means get well. re-cover would mean covering Gran again.

pool.prompt: A story has {b} two-word describing pairs that come before their noun, like well-known author, and {a} that come after their noun, like the author is well known. How many hyphens does it need?
pool.hint: Only the pairs that come before the noun get a hyphen.
pool.explain: Each of the {b} pairs before a noun gets one hyphen. The {a} pairs after a noun get none, so {b} hyphens in all.
